recognize_zh: 血片中一條細長、彎曲蜿蜒的線狀蟲體，長度相當於數十顆紅血球，體內有一列深紫色的體核，尾端逐漸變細，即血液中的微絲蟲（microfilaria）；鞘膜在此圖中不明顯，種別需看鞘與尾端核分布。
features: Very long, slender, thread-like larva spanning dozens of red cell diameters, with graceful serpentine curves
Body filled with a column of densely packed dark purple somatic nuclei
Tapering tail end; a nucleus-free tail tip is suggested but not clearly resolvable
Sheath not clearly distinguishable from the body at this magnification
Background of red cells with numerous neutrophils and scattered eosinophils
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single, very long and slender nematode larva with sinuous curves, containing a dense column of dark-staining somatic nuclei and tapering toward the tail. The sheath and the precise distribution of nuclei at the tail tip cannot be confidently assessed at this magnification. The background contains red cells, neutrophils and scattered eosinophils. Findings are consistent with a microfilaria; the described features favor Wuchereria bancrofti, but species identification rests on the presence of a sheath, the cephalic space and the nucleus-free tail, ideally confirmed on Giemsa-stained thick films or by antigen testing.

ddx.vs: Brugia microfilariae are sheathed with a sheath staining pink on Giemsa and have two distinct separate terminal nuclei at the tail tip.
Loa loa microfilariae are sheathed but have nuclei extending continuously to the tip of the tail and show diurnal periodicity.
Mansonella perstans microfilariae are small, unsheathed, and have nuclei extending to a bluntly rounded tail tip.
Artifactual fibers lack internal nuclei and the organized tapering head and tail of a larva.
